summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development first, made a new worktree, and correctly left the held tasks alone. It did not follow the empty-frontier procedure the story describes. It never ran `sdd-state next`, never posted a waiting record (`sdd-state wait --kind tasks`) and never printed the board. Instead it tried `sdd-state claim` on tasks 1 and 2, got status=held (exit=4) for both, and asked me whether to take one over. After my "No, the other session is still working." it handed back. No waiting/ directory exists in the cache.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 clearly fail. The session log shows no `sdd-state next`, `wait` or `board` calls, and there is no waiting/ directory in the cache. The agent did avoid --takeover and did hand back, but the core behaviour under test (post a waiting record, print the board, hand back) did not happen.

observations.description: The empty-frontier rule was not followed. When every task was held, the agent probed with `sdd-state claim` instead of `sdd-state next`, and posted no waiting record and no board. The text of the SDD skill as loaded never mentions the `next`, `wait` or `board` verbs, or waiting records. A grep of the log for 'waiting record', 'none reason' and 'kind tasks' found nothing. So the candidate skill may not document the rule at all, or keeps it in a reference file the agent never loads.

The agent wrote to the shared ledger directly with a shell heredoc: `cat >> .../progress.md <<EOF session ${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID}: mode worktree ...`. It did not go through an sdd-state verb, so the ledger got an unvalidated write.

After finding both tasks held, the agent offered 'Take over Task 2 only' and 'Take over both tasks' through AskUserQuestion. The story expected it to post a waiting record and hand back, not to suggest takeover options right away.

Claude Code's first-run flow showed a theme picker, security notes, a trust dialog, a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt (even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5) and a bypass-permissions warning. On the trust and bypass dialogs the default is 'No, exit'. On my first launch the Down keypress was apparently dropped and Claude exited, so I had to relaunch.
The worktree was created under .claude/worktrees/parallel on a new branch worktree-parallel. The plan is registered on feature/parallel, and the main checkout was on a detached HEAD.

criteria.criterion: SDD skill invoked before any other work
criteria.evidence: First tool_use in session log 060b8a78-...jsonl: "Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development", followed by "Skill: hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees".

criteria.criterion: Agent ran `sdd-state next` and output shows `none reason=held`
criteria.evidence: In the session log, the only sdd-state verbs used in Bash calls are sync, verify and claim. `grep -o 'sdd-state [a-z]*'` over the log returned claim/finish/handoff/prune/snapshot/sync/verify, with no `next`. The agent learned the tasks were held from `sdd-state claim ... 1` output: "status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ... exit=4" (same for task 2).

criteria.criterion: Waiting record of kind `tasks` posted; file under waiting/ holds kind=tasks
criteria.evidence: No `sdd-state wait` call anywhere in the log (same grep). `find $HOME/.cache -path '*waiting*'` returned nothing. The cache only has progress.md, claims/task-1/owner and claims/task-2/owner.
No `sdd-state board` in any Bash command in the session log (grep over the log shows no 'board' verb).

criteria.criterion: Agent handed back saying every task is held by another session
criteria.evidence: Final message on screen: "Understood. The other session is still working, so I'm leaving both claims alone and waiting for your instruction. This session took no tasks and dispatched nothing...". An earlier message said "both tasks are already held by fixture-session".

`grep -c -- '--takeover'` on the log returned 1. That one hit is in the loaded skill text ("take over (`--takeover`) only on their explicit yes"), not in a Bash command. The list of Bash tool_use commands from jq contains no --takeover.
